# Laboratory News

Welcome to the latest news from the **Roylawar Plant–Microbiome Research Laboratory**. Here we share research achievements, student accomplishments, publications, collaborations, internships, and other important laboratory milestones.

---

# 2026

## 📄 Publication Alert

We are delighted to share our recent publication:

**"Microbial allies in a cotton pest: A descriptive account of associated microbiota dynamics in *Dysdercus cingulatus* across development"**

published in **Comparative Biochemistry and Physiology Part D: Genomics and Proteomics**.

The study began with a scientific question aimed at understanding the microbial communities associated with the cotton pest *Dysdercus cingulatus*. Through experimental design, sequencing, microbiome analysis, data interpretation, and manuscript preparation, the project evolved into a valuable scientific contribution.

Congratulations to **Ms. Pravara Rupawate** for her dedication, scientific curiosity, and perseverance throughout the project.

Special congratulations to **Dr. Seema Borgave** for her continuous guidance, mentorship, and unwavering support in transforming this research idea into a published scientific contribution.

## 🇫🇮 Successful Completion of Ph.D. Research Visit

Ms. **Shreya Kasar** successfully completed her six-month Ph.D. research visit to the **Department of Microbiology, University of Helsinki, Finland**.

During her visit, she received advanced training in:

- Metagenomic data analysis
- Functional microbiome analysis
- Bioinformatics

The visit resulted in:

- Advanced expertise in microbiome bioinformatics
- Strengthened international research collaborations
- Significant progress toward her doctoral research
- Long-term collaborative opportunities between the collaborating institutions

---

## 🏆 Ph.D. Scholar Upgraded to Senior Research Fellow

Congratulations to **Ms. Avantika Jakati** on her successful upgradation to the position of **Senior Research Fellow (SRF)**.

This achievement recognizes her excellent research progress and continued contribution to her doctoral research on **plastic-degrading bacteria and antibiotic resistance in wastewater treatment sludge**.

## 🌱 Eight Students Join ICAR-DOGR Internship Programme

As the **MoU Coordinator** between our institution and **ICAR – Directorate of Onion and Garlic Research (ICAR-DOGR)**, I am pleased to share that **eight students from the Department of Botany** have joined the **three-month internship programme** at ICAR-DOGR.

The internship provides students with valuable hands-on training in modern agricultural research, laboratory techniques, and onion and garlic research.

---

## 🎉 NGSF Fellowship Award

Congratulations to **Ms. Lina Sonawane** on being selected for the **NGSF Fellowship** to undertake a **three-month internship programme at ICAR – Directorate of Onion and Garlic Research (ICAR-DOGR)**.

We wish her every success in her research journey.

# 2025

## 🎓 Prestigious EDUFI Fellowship & International Research Achievement

I am delighted to share a milestone that reflects the value of mentorship, collaboration, and perseverance.

My first Ph.D. student, **Ms. Shreya Kasar**, was awarded the prestigious **EDUFI Fellowship** by the **Finnish National Agency for Education**, enabling her to undertake a fully funded six-month research visit to the **Department of Microbiology, University of Helsinki, Finland**.

Through this fellowship, she completed a significant part of her doctoral research while receiving advanced training in metagenomics, functional microbiome analysis, and bioinformatics.

This achievement is particularly significant because:

- She is the **first Ph.D. student from our college** to complete a substantial part of her doctoral research through an international collaboration.
- She is the **first student from the Department of Botany under Savitribai Phule Pune University (SPPU)** to receive the prestigious **EDUFI Fellowship**.

This accomplishment reflects her dedication, perseverance, and scientific commitment, together with the continuous encouragement and support of our institution and collaborators.
